Question 1: Relationship between vehicle type and ride distance(maybe use facet_wrap for visualization)
Question 2: Relationship between driver rating and vehicle time of arrival

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```


```{r}

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
uber_data <- read.csv(" ")

head(uber_data)
summary(uber_data)
```


```{r}
uber_clean <- uber_data %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~na_if(., "null"))) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~na_if(., "NA"))) %>%

  mutate(
    Date = ymd(Date),
    Time = hms(Time),

    Avg.VTAT = as.numeric(Avg.VTAT),
    Avg.CTAT = as.numeric(Avg.CTAT),
    Cancelled.Rides.by.Customer = as.numeric(Cancelled.Rides.by.Customer),
    Incomplete.Rides = as.numeric(Incomplete.Rides),
    Booking.Value = as.numeric(Booking.Value),
    Ride.Distance = as.numeric(Ride.Distance),
    Driver.Ratings = as.numeric(Driver.Ratings),
    Customer.Rating = as.numeric(Customer.Rating),
    USD.Value = round(Booking.Value / 88.23, 2)
    
  )
head(uber_clean)
view(uber_clean)
```


```{r}
uber_clean <- uber_data[, -c(11, 12, 13, 14,15,16,21)]

view(uber_clean)
```

```{r}
cor(uber_clean$Driver.Ratings, uber_clean$Avg.VTAT, use = "complete.obs")
```



```{r}
#bekha


str(uber_clean)
library(scales)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyverse)


set.seed(123)  # for reproducibility
hourly_rates <- uber_clean %>%
  filter(
    Booking.Status == "Completed",
    Ride.Distance > 0,
    USD.Value > 0,
    !is.na(Vehicle.Type) # Safety check
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rate_km = USD.Value / Ride.Distance, # Create the price-per-km metric
    Hour = hour(Time)                  # Extract the hour from the Time
  ) %>%
  group_by(Vehicle.Type, Hour) %>%
  summarise(Median_Rate_Per_Km = median(rate_km), .groups = "drop") # Get the median rate




# 2. Now, plot the new 'hourly_rates' summary as a heatmap
ggplot(hourly_rates, aes(x = Hour, y = Vehicle.Type, fill = Median_Rate_Per_Km)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() + # A color scale that's good for heatmaps
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 23, by = 2)) +
  labs(
    title = "Price Efficiency (USD/km) by Vehicle Type and Hour",
    x = "Hour of the Day (0-23)",
    y = "Vehicle Type",
    fill = "Median USD/km"
  )




ggplot(hourly_rates, aes(x = Hour, y = Median_Rate_Per_Km)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +  # This creates the line chart
  facet_wrap(~ Vehicle.Type, scales = "free_y") + # This is the magic!
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 23, by = 4)) + # Cleaner x-axis
  labs(
    title = "Price Per Kilometer (USD) by Hour",
    subtitle = "Each vehicle type shows a different pricing pattern",
    x = "Hour of the Day (0-23)",
    y = "Median Price per Kilometer (USD)"
  )

```




```{r}
set.seed(123)

uber_sample <- uber_clean %>%
  drop_na(Avg.VTAT, Driver.Ratings) %>%
  sample_n(min(1000, n()))

ggplot(uber_sample, aes(x = Avg.VTAT, y = Driver.Ratings)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.3, color = "#0072B2", size = 2, width = 0.25, height = 0.05) +  
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "#D55E00", linewidth = 1.2, linetype = "solid") + 
  labs(
    title = "Driver Ratings vs Vehicle Arrival Time",
    subtitle = "Sample of 1,000 rides (negative trend suggests longer waits may lower ratings)",
    x = "Average Vehicle Time at Arrival (minutes)",
    y = "Driver Rating"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) + 
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, color = "gray30", hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray85"),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "gray20")
  )

```

```{r}
set.seed(123)

uber_sample <- uber_clean %>%
  drop_na(Avg.CTAT, Customer.Rating) %>%          
  sample_n(min(1000, n()))                        

ggplot(uber_sample, aes(x = Avg.CTAT, y = Customer.Rating)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.3, color = "#0072B2", size = 2, width = 0.25, height = 0.05) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "#D55E00", linewidth = 1.2) +         
  labs(
    title = "Customer Ratings vs Customer Arrival Time (CTAT)",
    subtitle = "Sample of 1,000 rides — longer customer wait times slightly reduce satisfaction",
    x = "Average Customer Time at Arrival (minutes)",
    y = "Customer Rating"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, color = "gray30", hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray85"),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "gray20")
  )
```
